placementGuidelines: VOLUNTEER-WEED, EMBRACE-DON'T-FIGHT: one of the most drought-tolerant, disease-resistant, low-input warm-season turf grasses available, but its distinctive Y-shaped black seed heads can shoot up an inch a day in summer, making a freshly mowed lawn look 'weedy' again within 48 hours. Rather than fighting the biology, work with it: those rapid seed heads are effectively free, continuous overseeding that thickens thin turf over a couple of seasons and helps crowd out harsher weeds. Raising the mower deck to 3-4 in. encourages deeper roots and helps new seed stalks blend in visually; a Plant Growth Regulator (e.g., trinexapac-ethyl) can cut seed-head/mowing frequency roughly in half if a tidier look is wanted without giving up the grass's toughness. For an intentional low-maintenance pasture/meadow look, mow only every 2-3 weeks at the highest deck setting and consider overseeding with White or Crimson Clover in fall - clover fixes nitrogen into the Bahia's roots for free and adds a pollinator-friendly bloom layer over winter. If grazing small livestock, keep growth managed to 2-6 in. for better forage digestibility; unmanaged, fully mature stockpiled growth builds a dense, weed-choking sod but is lower quality forage.
